ai.description: *Takydromus sikkimensis* reaches 20 cm total length. It is olive-brown with a distinct white lateral stripe and possesses four inguinal pores and three pairs of chin shields. Family: Lacertidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Sikkim Grass Lizard is best distinguished by the presence of only two pairs of chin shields, whereas most other Indian *Takydromus* species possess three or more pairs.
ai.habitat: The Sikkim Grass Lizard inhabits moist, high-altitude temperate forests and grassy slopes in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sikkim grass lizard is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects among grasses and low vegetation while utilizing its long, prehensile tail for balance.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Takydromus sikkimensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Takydromus sikkimensis* is endemic to the Eastern Himalayas, primarily inhabiting Sikkim and West Bengal at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
